title: Legislative districts of Iligan

{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2022}} {{Use Philippine English|date=July 2022}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Iligan''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Iligan]] in the [[Congress of the Philippines]]. The city is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the Congress through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Lanao|Legislative districts of Lanao del Norte}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Iligan were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935), the historical [[Lanao (province)|Lanao Province]] (1935–1961), [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XII]] (1978–1984) and [[Lanao del Norte]] (1961–1972; 1987–2010). By virtue of being classified as a [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] in 1983, Iligan was granted separate representation for the first time in the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]], electing [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, at large]], in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. However, under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the city was grouped again with Lanao del Norte and placed in its [[Legislative districts of Lanao del Norte#1987–2010|first congressional district]];{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|accessdate=November 21, 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} this district elected its first representative to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. [[Iligan]] regained separate representation with the passage of Republic Act No. 9724 on October 20, 2009, which segregated the city from the [[Legislative districts of Lanao del Norte#1987–2010|first district of Lanao del Norte]] to form its [[#Lone District|own congressional district]] starting in the [[2010 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2010 elections]].{{cite web|url=http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209724.pdf|title=Republic Act No. 9724 - An Act Separating the City of Iligan from the First Legislative District of the Province of Lanao del Norte to Constitute the Lone Legislative District of the City of Iligan|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=October 20, 2009|accessdate=February 18, 2017|website=Senate of the Philippines}} == Lone District == *'''Population (2015)''': 342,618{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|accessdate=November 21, 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
